<section_guide number="1" title="Overview">
<purpose>Define product vision, document name, target users, core problem, solution strategy, success criteria, and differentiators</purpose>

<questions>
1. What is the main purpose of the project? (→ 1.1)
2. Confirm the document name (default: the project name provided at init). (→ 1.2)
3. Who are the target users? (→ 1.3)
4. What is the core problem to solve? (→ 1.4)
5. What is the solution strategy? (→ 1.5)
6. What criteria will determine whether the product is successful? (→ 1.6)
7. What are the key differentiators vs. alternatives? (→ 1.7)
</questions>

<note>
1.6 Success Criteria is a high-level, possibly qualitative signal of product success (e.g. "users adopt it as their primary tool"). It is distinct from Section 2's KPIs, which are the measurable MVP-validation targets. Keep 1.6 at the vision level; the numbers belong in Section 2.
</note>

<example>
### 1.1 Purpose

- Enable users to automatically generate technical/functional specification documents by conversing with AI
- Help developers, product managers, and planners write MVP technical specs more efficiently

### 1.2 Document Name

- ALPS (PRD) Writer

### 1.3 Target Users

- Developers, product managers, and planners who need to write MVP specs quickly

### 1.4 Core Problem

- Writing a complete, unambiguous PRD is slow and quality depends heavily on the author's skill

### 1.5 Solution Strategy

- An AI agent drives the authoring loop, asking focused questions section by section

### 1.6 Success Criteria

- Users can produce a usable MVP spec in a single guided session

### 1.7 Key Differentiators

- The agent asks, the human answers — quality is bounded by the template, not the author's PRD-writing skill
  </example>

<completion>Present one concise plain-text approval digest covering all seven subsections 1.1–1.7, including every contract-bearing value, scope boundary, and success condition, then get user confirmation. Save each approved subsection separately.</completion>
</section_guide>
